result.summary: 'attempted' is the single largest applicable-cell fate on the live server: 8,771 of ~22,458 applicable cells (39.1%) across tenant_xbow, vs 25.0% resolved and 35.9% open. But the attempt-cap machinery is NOT why cells strand there — na_reason shows 8,683/8,771 (99.0%) reached 'attempted' via finalize.py's scanner_finalize_retire_unreached sweep (never-genuinely-probed untested/methods-less-testing cells retired at scan end so count_open_cells can hit 0), and only 82 (0.9%) via the genuine attempt-cap. The deployed cap is 6 (SCANNER_LEDGER_ATTEMPT_CAP=6), not the code default 3. So 'attempted' is honestly labeled terminal (father _TERMINAL_STATES #30 fix confirmed; report gives it its own bucket, excluded from resolved_pct) but its real meaning is "the fleet never drained the grid before the scan ended" — a throughput-vs-grid-size coverage ceiling, not per-cell exhaustion. Per-scan this ranges 40–93% attempted on large grids (2122→40%, 768→93%) and 0% on small fully-drained grids (39→100% resolved). Two honesty defects fall out: the report and live board both label the whole attempted bucket "attempt-capped"/"done", conflating 8,683 never-reached cells with 82 genuinely-tried ones; and the deployed lease (1800s) is far below the worker wall (86400s), violating the code's documented lease-must-exceed-wall invariant and inflating attempts via mid-run reclaim.

questions.answer: _OPEN_STATES=('untested','testing') at service.py:50; there is no _DONE_STATES in ledger/service.py (that constant lives in father.py:376). Attempt cap = _attempt_cap() at service.py:1237-1247, reads SCANNER_LEDGER_ATTEMPT_CAP, CODE DEFAULT 3 (comment 'was 0'), cap<=0 = legacy unbounded. Mechanism: claim_cells (service.py:1388-1417) increments attempts on each claim and filters 'AND c.attempts < :cap' so a capped cell is no longer claimable; it is absorbed to terminal 'attempted' only via release_cells (:1460), release_cells_by_ids (:1492), or reclaim_expired_leases (:1559), each 'state = CASE WHEN attempts >= :cap THEN attempted'. count_claimable_cells (:1508-1521) also filters attempts<cap → quiescence signal. questions.q: DO-2: father.py _TERMINAL_STATES (~:378) / _render_board_totals (~:436) — is 'attempted' terminal/resolved or dropped? (CLAUDE.md #30 says fixed)
questions.answer: CONFIRMED FIXED. father.py:376 _DONE_STATES=frozenset{tested_clean,confirmed,blocked}; :378 _TERMINAL_STATES=_DONE_STATES|{'attempted'}. So 'attempted' is counted, in the 'done' bucket — NOT dropped. Caveat/defect: the live board LUMPS attempted into 'done' (done = tested_clean+confirmed+blocked+attempted per the :388 docstring), so mid/late-run 'done N' overstates genuinely-tested cells by the whole attempted pile (39% tenant-wide).

defects.title: Deployed lease (1800s) is far below the worker wall (86400s), inverting the code's documented lease>wall invariant
defects.mechanism: service.py:1227-1234 states the lease must EXCEED SCANNER_ENGINE_WORKER_WALL_S (+600s margin) so reclaim_expired_leases only fires for a genuinely dead/hung worker, never mid-run. Deployed: SCANNER_LEDGER_LEASE_S=1800 (30min) vs SCANNER_ENGINE_WORKER_WALL_S=86400 (24h). A live worker legitimately holding a cell past 30min has it reclaimed and re-claimed (attempts+1) repeatedly, inflating attempts (histogram shows 647 cells at attempts>=4 under cap=6) and risking premature cap-absorb to 'attempted' while the worker is still working it (double-work).

A sustained flap burns the per-cell attempt cap on cells that were never actually tested, absorbing them to 'attempted' so count_claimable->0 and the wave loop legitimately terminates with untested surface marked attempted — a genuine 'cut scans short' pathway via the preempt path, not the loop-stop path. LATENT: cell_states_failed=0 across all prod logs; narrow trigger (partial DB failure). NOT tracked in CLAUDE.md (distinct from the already-fixed count_claimable/has_claimable CRITICAL). Lazy root-cause fix: treat an empty cell_states result for a non-empty id list as 'unknown -> return None (keep working)' rather than 'satisfied' at father.py:1310.

defects.title: target_health() fails open to 1.0 with zero logging, silently defeating fleet concurrency-shedding

A DB/telemetry read error therefore reads as 'perfectly healthy', pinning the cap at hard_cap; a persistent outage is indistinguishable from a healthy target and no log line records it.
defects.blast_radius: Concurrency-shedding is silently disabled during a telemetry outage, so the fleet keeps full worker concurrency against a target that may be struggling (more transport failures, wasted budget, possible false 'unreachable' findings). Direction is OVER-drive, not early-stop — it does not shorten scans and is not an H1 quiescence risk. Already tracked in CLAUDE.md Known Issues, but that entry's detail 'the file imports no logger at all' is now STALE (structlog imported at :7, logger at :25 and used by count_claimable); only target_health's except block still lacks logging. Live on the prod batch-dispatch path. Lazy fix: add one logger.awarning in the except, mirroring count_claimable.

defects.title: Coverage-complete stop fires at 98% resolved, leaving up to 2% of applicable cells genuinely open (design fact, not an error-path fail-open)

result.summary: Wall-time in an Abhedi Red engine-v2 scan is overwhelmingly spent in the DISPATCH phase (worker LLM execution), not in ledger/sync overhead. The wave loop is Father.run()'s `while True` (father.py:1762): per iteration it does materialize (1 DB grid upsert), a serial wave-boundary sync (ingest+resolve+census+dedup), claim (one SKIP-LOCKED round-trip, limit 72), then dispatch — and dispatch is where all worker LLM time lives. In prod (compose pins batch_dispatch=true, stuck_window=300s) the MAIN wave runs through the rolling run_pool (hard_cap=4, 300s stuck-cut), but the exploit floor (budget 1500s) and periodic sync (120s) run CONCURRENTLY with it and are cancelled on return, so they overlap rather than add. The real cost multiplier is the per-worker reprompt loop (agents_runtime.py:812-838): up to max_reprompts(6)+1 iterations x max_turns(40) = ~280 Runner turns per worker, each re-feeding the full capped transcript (growing context on a non-caching proxied model). Live evidence: decisions.log is 100% `max_turns_exceeded` (65/65) with workers reaching ·turn7, and the live 7.5h scan's ledger has 1704 cells stuck in `testing` limbo vs only 964 resolved — workers grind turns without recording terminal coverage, the stuck-watchdog counts tool_calls as "progress" so never cuts them, leases expire and cells re-test = coverage thrash that prevents quiescence. Scan durations span 321s to 64,395s (17.9h), with a heavy right tail of multi-hour runaways. H1 (slow scans = ledger/sync overhead) is REFUTED: slowness is worker-LLM turn-grind + testing-limbo thrash + run_all barriers for escalation, not ledger writes.

questions.q: Which wave-loop phase dominates wall-time and why?
questions.answer: DISPATCH dominates (~95%+). Mechanism: dispatch is the only phase that runs worker LLM loops; each worker grinds up to ~280 Runner turns (6 reprompts x 40 turns, agents_runtime.py:809+326+812-838) because the offensive-gate rarely trips on the weak proxied model (bunny) — decisions.log is 100% max_turns_exceeded. materialize/claim/wave-boundary-sync are single bounded DB round-trips; the exploit floor (1500s budget) and periodic sync (120s) run concurrently (create_task) with the wave and are cancelled on return (father.py:1100-1106,1395-1416), so they overlap dispatch rather than add to it.

questions.q: H1: are slow scans caused by ledger/sync overhead rather than coverage genuinely taking time?
questions.answer: REFUTED (with nuance). Ledger/sync is cheap and mostly concurrent: wave-boundary _sync_work_to_db is one serial DB pass (father.py:1770,888-967); periodic_sync (120s) overlaps the wave. Slowness is (a) worker LLM turn-grind in dispatch, and (b) coverage THRASH — 1704 of 2989 applicable cells sit in `testing` limbo (live QUERY) because workers never record terminal coverage, so count_claimable never drains and the loop runs to max_waves/wall. It is neither pure ledger overhead NOR honest coverage time; it is WASTED worker time (turns that don't terminalize cells) re-paid across waves. The one sync-adjacent real cost — live_convergence verify(LLM)+report-regen on the 120s tick (father.py:1050-1075) — is throttled (180s) and concurrent, a secondary bandwidth competitor, not the driver.

questions.q: Does prod actually use the rolling run_pool or the run_all gather-barrier?

But escalation (_run_escalation, father.py:1720), authed-recrawl (:1575), auth-bootstrap (:1515) and smoke workers (:1483) all call fleet.run_all -> _one -> asyncio.wait_for(wall) with NO stuck-watchdog (fleet.py:74-76,121-122). This is where essentially all dispatch wall-time is spent.

defects.title: Coverage thrash: 1704 cells stuck in `testing` limbo because workers grind turns without recording terminal coverage, and the loop cannot quiesce

result.role: WS-1 Per-worker wall and scan time-cap auditor (Abhedi Red / autocan, pkg scanner, branch feat/alpha-observability @ f75608f)
result.summary: The platform has four time backstops (per-worker wall, Manager stuck-watchdog, scan-level runaway wall, and an opt-in scan time_cap), but all sit BEHIND the Governor progress signals (coverage-complete OR plateau), so by design a healthy scan stops on work-done, not the clock. The single most important finding is a code-vs-deployed drift: scanner-cp actually runs SCANNER_ENGINE_WORKER_WALL_S=86400 and SCANNER_ENGINE_RUNAWAY_WALL_S=86400 (both 24h) via docker-compose.override.yml, NOT the code defaults (5400s/90min worker, 21600s/6h runaway) nor the tracked compose pins, so the ~90 min per-worker wall in code comments and docs effectively NEVER fires in production. Live DB evidence REFUTES wall/cap dominance: of 22 time-capped scans only 1 (5%) reached its cap (a graceful partial at 106% of cap), while the other 21 finished at 7-44% of cap; uncapped scans span 1.5 min to 17.9h and completed under the 24h ceiling on coverage/plateau. A per-worker wall hit does NOT lose findings (in-process asyncio.wait_for timeout returning a partial WorkerResult with /work already flushed). The genuine finding-loss risk is the time-cap/cancel graceful path, which SIGKILLs at the 120s finalize-grace ceiling (observed live twice on 2026-09-30), cutting in-flight finalize work, though per-wave flush and salvage preserve already-proven findings.

questions.q: Q2: How is the wall enforced (SIGKILL / graceful drain / finalize-on-timeout)? Does a wall-hit lose in-flight findings/coverage?
questions.answer: Two mechanisms. (a) Per-worker wall: IN-PROCESS asyncio.wait_for(w.run, timeout=_worker_wall_s()) [fleet.py:76,89] plus a monotonic deadline on the preempt path [fleet.py:97-107]; on hit TimeoutError to WorkerResult(status=partial) [fleet.py:60-66]. NO SIGKILL, NO finding loss (/work already flushed, cells re-queue via on_done). (b) Scan time_cap: primary graceful stopper is the in-container soft-cap [father.py:852-887] tripping wrap_up at cap-margin, breaking the wave loop [father.py:1771-1774] AFTER a per-wave /work-to-DB flush [father.py:1767-1770], finalizing with toolserver alive. Backstop: poller elapsed>time_cap_seconds to _cancel_scan(graceful=True) [poller.py:1217-1227] drops /work/close.json, SIGTERM, waits up to SCANNER_FINALIZE_GRACE_S 120s via _drain_or_kill, SIGKILL at ceiling [poller.py:955-972,997-1002], then salvage-finalize [poller.py:1034-1040]. FINDING LOSS bounded but real: findings.jsonl entries survive (per-wave flush plus salvage); in-flight findings and the whole finalize pass (verify/enrich/report-regen) lost if it overruns 120s. CONFIRMED live: cancel_sigkill_sent grace_s=120.0 fired exactly 120s after SIGTERM on two 2026-09-30 stops [QUERY docker logs].

questions.q: Q3: Is the non-anthropic uncapped path (SCANNER_NONANTHROPIC_DEFAULT_TIME_CAP_S) truly unlimited?
questions.answer: YES. resolve_time_cap(None,...) returns None unless BOTH non_anthropic AND default_s>0 [scans.py:83-87]. Field defaults 0 [config.py:464], compose default 0 [docker-compose.yml:226], DEPLOYED 0 [QUERY]. With cap None the poller check is skipped (guarded by time_cap_seconds truthiness [poller.py:1217]) and the soft-cap is off (SCANNER_TIME_CAP_S only forwarded when >0 [worker.py:871-872]; _soft_cap_s None when cap<=0 [father.py:860-862]). Only residual bounds are the deployed 24h runaway and 24h worker wall. Live: running scan 84aea81a (bunny/OpenRouter, non-Anthropic) has time_cap NULL at 114.7min [QUERY].

questions.q: Q4: For recent scans, how many ended at/near the cap vs finished naturally?
questions.answer: tenant_xbow: 41 scans (18 completed, 17 cancelled, 4 failed, 1 partial, 1 running). Of 22 with a time_cap (mostly 2100s/35min, one 900s): ONLY 1 (5%) reached cap, a partial at 106% (2225s vs 2100s; the ~125s overrun equals SIGTERM plus finalize-grace, confirming the graceful path not a hard kill-at-cap). Other 21 at 7-44% of cap [QUERY pct_of_cap]. Uncapped durations 91s to 64395s (17.9h); two longest (17.9h, 15.2h) COMPLETED under the 24h wall [QUERY]. Recent cap/wall log events are user cancels, not poller.time_cap_exceeded [QUERY]. Neither cap nor wall dominates on this deployment; work completes/plateaus first.

defects.title: Deployed 24h worker and runaway walls contradict code (90min/6h) and compose pins; the no-backstops intent is only half-realized (86400 is a finite wall, not the 0 sentinel)
defects.mechanism: docker-compose.override.yml sets SCANNER_ENGINE_WORKER_WALL_S=86400 and SCANNER_ENGINE_RUNAWAY_WALL_S=86400 [QUERY scanner-cp env]. Code default worker wall 5400s [fleet.py:28], runaway 21600s [context.py:115]; Governor treats a positive max_wall_s as a live cap so 86400 STILL fires the runaway partial at 24h [governor.py:46]. The 6h runaway wall was added to close the 12h-runaway class; overriding to 24h re-widens it. Because 86400 is not 0, the override header wall/time caps removed is inaccurate - they are stretched, not removed.
defects.blast_radius: A wedged worker or runaway scan can burn up to 24h of container/LLM/compute before any clock reaps it (the lease also stretches to ~24h10m [ledger/service.py:1233], so orphaned cells stay claimed that long). Conversely an XBOW run legitimately needing >24h silently walls out despite uncapped intent. Code comments (worker.py:862-863 ~90min), FLAGS.md, CONFIG_TRUTH_TABLE.md and any agent reasoning from them are stale about the real bound.
defects.module_flag: docker-compose.override.yml -> SCANNER_ENGINE_WORKER_WALL_S / SCANNER_ENGINE_RUNAWAY_WALL_S (both 86400); conflicting .env WORKER_WALL=9000 shadowed

defects.title: Time-cap / cancel graceful stop hard-SIGKILLs at the 120s finalize-grace ceiling, cutting in-flight finalize (verify/enrich/report-regen) and not-yet-flushed findings
defects.mechanism: _cancel_scan(graceful=True) drops /work/close.json, SIGTERMs, then _drain_or_kill waits up to SCANNER_FINALIZE_GRACE_S (default/deployed 120s) and SIGKILLs at the ceiling [poller.py:955-972,997-1002]. If the in-container close-sweep+finalize (A1 verifier + enrich + report regen) cannot finish in 120s it is killed mid-pass. Observed live: cancel_sigkill_sent grace_s=120.0 exactly 120s after SIGTERM on two 2026-09-30 stops [QUERY docker logs]. Time-cap uses the identical path.
defects.blast_radius: Already-proven findings survive (per-wave /work-to-DB flush [father.py:1767-1770] plus poller salvage [poller.py:1034-1040]), so not the total loss of the old bug; but the final verify/enrich/report pass and any finding computed-but-unflushed at the kill instant are lost, degrading a stopped scan report vs a clean finish. Widening SCANNER_FINALIZE_GRACE_S, or gating the SIGKILL on the finalizing.json marker for the graceful (non-hung) case, shrinks the window.

defects.title: Stuck-watchdog (deployed 20min; code default DISABLED) can preempt a worker legitimately blocked on a single long tool, causing preempt+requeue thrash
defects.mechanism: _batch_done marks a worker stuck when for _stuck_window_s there is no new terminal cell, no fresher cells_last_progress, AND no tool_calls increment [father.py:1318-1336]. A worker running ONE long tool (sqlmap dump, ffuf, nuclei) spanning the window increments none of these and is cut with stuck: no progress. Code default is 0 DISABLED specifically to avoid this (cutting the latter discards real in-flight work, strictly worse [father.py:532-534]); deploy overrides ON at 1200s (compose pins 300s).
defects.blast_radius: Bounded: the deployed 20-min window tolerates most single tools and on a cut the cells re-queue via on_done work-stealing with /work persisted - cost is rework/thrash and lost partial tool progress, not proven-finding loss. At the compose-pinned 300s (5min) the risk is materially higher for any real DAST tool. Same coverage-thrash class the 2026-09-17 fix targeted; the tool-aware signal only helps a worker that streams multiple tools within the window.

defects.title: Soft-cap graceful drain silently self-disables for any scan whose time_cap <= SOFT_CAP_MARGIN_S (180s)
defects.mechanism: _soft_cap_s returns None when cap <= margin [father.py:864], so a scan capped at <=180s gets NO in-container graceful drain and depends entirely on the poller SIGTERM->120s->SIGKILL backstop (the harsher, finding-lossier path) with zero log/warning that the drain was skipped.
defects.blast_radius: Narrow: only sub-3-minute caps (none in tenant_xbow history); but for such a scan the graceful-drain protections (clean wave-loop exit, toolserver-alive finalize) are all bypassed and the SIGKILL-mid-finalize window (Defect 2) becomes the only path.

hypotheses.id: H1: A per-worker wall (~90 min) and/or scan time caps DOMINATE the schedule (vs work genuinely completing).
hypotheses.note: Refuted on two axes. (1) The ~90min wall is a code default NOT deployed - prod runs 24h worker + 24h runaway walls [QUERY], so the wall almost never fires. (2) Live history: 21/22 capped scans finished at 7-44% of cap (only 1 at 106%), and uncapped scans complete on coverage/plateau up to 17.9h under the 24h ceiling. Governor stops on progress (unresolved==0 or plateau) ahead of every clock [governor.py:32-48]. Schedule is work-dominated.

hypotheses.id: H1a: A wall/cap hit loses in-flight findings via SIGKILL-before-flush.
hypotheses.note: Per-worker wall does NOT (asyncio timeout to partial, /work flushed) [fleet.py:60-66]. The time-cap/cancel graceful path DOES have a real SIGKILL-at-120s window cutting in-flight finalize, confirmed live [docker logs 2026-09-30]. Already-proven findings survive via per-wave flush plus salvage; findings not yet in findings.jsonl at the kill instant are lost.

hypotheses.id: H1b: The non-anthropic uncapped path is truly unlimited.
hypotheses.note: default_s=0 in code, compose, and deployment; resolve_time_cap returns None; only the deployed 24h walls bound it [scans.py:83-87, config.py:464, QUERY].

gaps: proxy_log.db (logging-proxy) covers only NVIDIA/nemotron; the live scan and other OpenRouter/bunny scans bypass it, so per-turn timing/cost telemetry for those runs was not cross-checkable - durations here come from DB started_at/completed_at only.

The single time-capped scan that reached its cap (partial at 106%) predates the retained scanner-cp log window, so its exact poller.time_cap_exceeded to drain to terminal-status line was not readable; the 106% (~cap+125s = cap+finalize-grace) is inferred from DB duration, corroborated by the identical 120s grace seen on the two 2026-09-30 cancels.

Whether the 17.9h/15.2h completed scans were resumed (SCANNER_ENGINE_RESUME) vs one continuous run was not determined from started_at/completed_at alone; if resumed, per-segment wall reasoning is unaffected but the wall-clock span is not a single-scan bound.

I did not measure real DAST tool durations to quantify how often a single tool exceeds the deployed 1200s stuck window (Defect 3) vs the 300s compose pin - the risk is established from code semantics, not a measured preempt-rate; no engine-level test covers _batch_done single-long-tool case.
